properties.name: Finexus
properties.description:
Finexus – Where Banks Meet Innovation

Finexus is a next-generation Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that empowers banks and fintech companies to launch new digital financial services faster, securely, and at scale.

Built on more than a decade of Al Faris International Group’s leadership in mission-critical banking integrations, Finexus offers 260+ Saudi-ready APIs that cover payments, lending, deposits, cards, wallets, trade finance, supply chain finance, payroll, collections, investments, and more. These APIs are fully aligned with Open Banking, Open Finance, and ISO 20022 standards, ensuring compliance with SAMA regulations and global frameworks.

Finexus is multi-tenant by design. This means individual bank departments (retail, corporate, SME) can run their own APIs with full data isolation, while external fintechs and third-party providers can also host services on the same platform under secure governance and revenue-sharing models.

The platform comes with a full ecosystem of tools:
Developer Portal – Interactive API documentation, sandbox testing, SDKs, and developer support.
Self-Service Portal for TPPs – Onboarding, consent and credential management, real-time analytics, and regulatory compliance tools.
Admin Portal for Banks – TPP approval, API lifecycle management, monitoring, fraud detection, billing, and subscription management.
Advanced Modules – Consent management (web & mobile SDKs), analytics dashboards, charging & billing engines, and marketplace integration for fintech, insuretech, agritech, and more.

With its SaaS deployment model, Finexus can run on leading cloud infrastructures with active-active disaster recovery, ensuring reliability and scalability.

By combining speed, flexibility, compliance, and monetization, Finexus helps banks modernize their digital offerings, enables fintechs to innovate, and creates new revenue streams through an open financial marketplace.

By transforming fragmented systems into a unified infrastructure, Cresora enables organizations to move money more intelligently, operate more efficiently, and achieve financial truth at scale.

entity.name: Finexus
entity.description:
Finexus – Where Banks Meet Innovation

Finexus is a next-generation Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that empowers banks and fintech companies to launch new digital financial services faster, securely, and at scale.

Built on more than a decade of Al Faris International Group’s leadership in mission-critical banking integrations, Finexus offers 260+ Saudi-ready APIs that cover payments, lending, deposits, cards, wallets, trade finance, supply chain finance, payroll, collections, investments, and more. These APIs are fully aligned with Open Banking, Open Finance, and ISO 20022 standards, ensuring compliance with SAMA regulations and global frameworks.

Finexus is multi-tenant by design. This means individual bank departments (retail, corporate, SME) can run their own APIs with full data isolation, while external fintechs and third-party providers can also host services on the same platform under secure governance and revenue-sharing models.

The platform comes with a full ecosystem of tools:
Developer Portal – Interactive API documentation, sandbox testing, SDKs, and developer support.
Self-Service Portal for TPPs – Onboarding, consent and credential management, real-time analytics, and regulatory compliance tools.
Admin Portal for Banks – TPP approval, API lifecycle management, monitoring, fraud detection, billing, and subscription management.
Advanced Modules – Consent management (web & mobile SDKs), analytics dashboards, charging & billing engines, and marketplace integration for fintech, insuretech, agritech, and more.

With its SaaS deployment model, Finexus can run on leading cloud infrastructures with active-active disaster recovery, ensuring reliability and scalability.

By combining speed, flexibility, compliance, and monetization, Finexus helps banks modernize their digital offerings, enables fintechs to innovate, and creates new revenue streams through an open financial marketplace.

AI is embedded at the core of Cresora, powering data normalization, transaction matching, anomaly detection, and operational insights. This reduces manual work, accelerates financial close, and improves visibility across operations.

Cresora is processor-agnostic and bank-agnostic, giving organizations the flexibility to scale without being locked into a single provider. Its modular architecture supports enterprises, software platforms, and partner ecosystems that require control, compliance, and precision.

By transforming fragmented systems into a unified infrastructure, Cresora enables organizations to move money more intelligently, operate more efficiently, and achieve financial truth at scale.

properties.name: Cresora Commerce
properties.description:
Cresora Commerce is an AI-native commerce infrastructure platform built for organizations operating in complex, high-volume, and regulated environments.

Modern commerce has outgrown traditional payment systems. Businesses today manage multiple transaction channels, fragmented financial data, and increasing pressure for speed, accuracy, and auditability. Legacy platforms were not designed for this level of complexity. They process transactions, but they do not orchestrate them.

Cresora solves this by acting as the infrastructure layer that connects systems, orchestrates transaction flow, and reconciles financial activity across the entire commerce lifecycle.

The platform unifies embedded commerce, omnichannel interaction, and financial reconciliation into a single framework. It enables organizations to route transactions across multiple processors, align data across systems, and achieve financial accuracy without manual reconciliation or rigid dependencies.

AI is embedded at the core of Cresora, powering data normalization, transaction matching, anomaly detection, and operational insights. This reduces manual work, accelerates financial close, and improves visibility across operations.

Cresora is processor-agnostic and bank-agnostic, giving organizations the flexibility to scale without being locked into a single provider. Its modular architecture supports enterprises, software platforms, and partner ecosystems that require control, compliance, and precision.

By transforming fragmented systems into a unified infrastructure, Cresora enables organizations to move money more intelligently, operate more efficiently, and achieve financial truth at scale.

# Trudenty (Trudenty Limited)

Trudenty is a Technology, Information and Internet company. Trudenty is a company that provides a consumer trust network for fraud risk intelligence across the commerce and payments ecosystem. They enable merchants, issuers, psps, and acquirers to collaborate to fight fraud across the commerce and payments ecosystem. Trudenty employs 4 people (+14.3% YoY, +1 person), founded in 2022. Headquartered in United Kingdom. Its workforce is distributed across United Kingdom and Luxembourg. Has $591.3K in total funding, with 2 prior funding rounds.

## About

Trudenty’s C

properties.name: Trudenty
properties.description:
Trudenty’s Consumer Trust Network helps merchants, issuers, acquirers, and processors collaborate through data sharing to prevent first-party and APP fraud. The network provides a 360 view of a consumer’s fraud risk for friendly fraud, without exposing personal or transactional data.

At its core, the Consumer Trust Index is a score that identifies trusted customers and differentiates them from potential fraudsters. This score provides companies with a view of how their customers act beyond their network, enabling the detection of fraudsters operating outside their network before they cause harm.

With the Consumer Trust Network, companies can make more effective reimbursement/refund decisions, resolve disputes faster and with less manual work, and prevent policy abuse, whilst preventing fraud losses from friendly fraud. By helping companies identify trustworthy customers and fraudsters, the Trust Index also supports businesses build trust with loyal customers and support growth.

The Trust Index is built using fraud insights shared by network members, combined with Open Banking and third-party data to close the visibility gap in fraud prevention. Through the Trust Network Protocol, peers can securely share and access consumer fraud risk insights while keeping the underlying data private. Members gain the benefits of shared intelligence without seeing the personal or transactional data behind it.

Unlike traditional systems that centralise data, Trudenty leverages shared infrastructure, so businesses keep control and ownership of their data. This type of open network enables data sharing of fraud risk signals whilst ensuring privacy and maintaining confidentiality for network members and consumers.

properties.name: Payment Solutions
properties.description:
Whether you are looking to process payments from customers or you want to make payments to them, we can manage all your payment processing requirements.

We are a BACS Approved Bureau and as registered Data Controllers and Processors we have the highest standards of data security and control. 

BACS Bureau status means we are able we are able to make payments direct to consumer bank accounts, including directly from client accounts where appropriate. MRM currently makes payments on behalf of the Government with direct access to their bank account, which is testament to our system security. 

Our secure payment processing facilities also allow us to take payments via credit & debit cards, cheque, postal order and direct debit as well as via invoices. We can also facilitate regular payments in Euros/Sterling & have experience in international payment advice in both Sterling and local currencies. 

For data security, bank account details are validated using web services and any bank details captured online are protected by encryption, using SSL digital certificates.

For any staff dealing with payments, experience in a similar secure environment is always preferred (for example, in handling cash/money off next purchase vouchers) where a high degree of trust and confidentiality is proven.

entity.name: Finexus

Finexus – Where Banks Meet Innovation

Finexus is a next-generation Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that empowers banks and fintech companies to launch new digital financial services faster, securely, and at scale.

Built on more than a decade of Al Faris International Group’s leadership in mission-critical banking integrations, Finexus offers 260+ Saudi-ready APIs that cover payments, lending, deposits, cards, wallets, trade finance, supply chain finance, payroll, collections, investments, and more. These APIs are fully aligned with Open Banking, Open Finance, and ISO 20022 standards, ensuring compliance with SAMA regulations and global frameworks.

Finexus is multi-tenant by design. This means individual bank departments (retail, corporate, SME) can run their own APIs with full data isolation, while external fintechs and third-party providers can also host services on the same platform under secure governance and revenue-sharing models.

Developer Portal – Interactive API documentation, sandbox testing, SDKs, and developer support.
Self-Service Portal for TPPs – Onboarding, consent and credential management, real-time analytics, and regulatory compliance tools.
Admin Portal for Banks – TPP approval, API lifecycle management, monitoring, fraud detection, billing, and subscription management.
Advanced Modules – Consent management (web & mobile SDKs), analytics dashboards, charging & billing engines, and marketplace integration for fintech, insuretech, agritech, and more.

With its SaaS deployment model, Finexus can run on leading cloud infrastructures with active-active disaster recovery, ensuring reliability and scalability.

By combining speed, flexibility, compliance, and monetization, Finexus helps banks modernize their digital offerings, enables fintechs to innovate, and creates new revenue streams through an open financial marketplace.

entity.name: Cresora Commerce
entity.description:
Cresora Commerce is an AI-native commerce infrastructure platform built for organizations operating in complex, high-volume, and regulated environments.

Modern commerce has outgrown traditional payment systems. Businesses today manage multiple transaction channels, fragmented financial data, and increasing pressure for speed, accuracy, and auditability. Legacy platforms were not designed for this level of complexity. They process transactions, but they do not orchestrate them.

Cresora solves this by acting as the infrastructure layer that connects systems, orchestrates transaction flow, and reconciles financial activity across the entire commerce lifecycle.

The platform unifies embedded commerce, omnichannel interaction, and financial reconciliation into a single framework. It enables organizations to route transactions across multiple processors, align data across systems, and achieve financial accuracy without manual reconciliation or rigid dependencies.

AI is embedded at the core of Cresora, powering data normalization, transaction matching, anomaly detection, and operational insights. This reduces manual work, accelerates financial close, and improves visibility across operations.

Cresora is processor-agnostic and bank-agnostic, giving organizations the flexibility to scale without being locked into a single provider. Its modular architecture supports enterprises, software platforms, and partner ecosystems that require control, compliance, and precision.

By transforming fragmented systems into a unified infrastructure, Cresora enables organizations to move money more intelligently, operate more efficiently, and achieve financial truth at scale.

Result: Recipient gets FIAT seamlessly; consumer pays with their chosen asset.

Connecting the Ecosystem
Our ecosystem connects via secure APIs:
• 𝗔𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀: Exchanges, Brokers, Loyalty Programs, Banks, Gaming Platforms, etc.

𝗦𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗲 & 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗯𝘆 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻

entity.name: Trudenty
entity.description:
Trudenty’s Consumer Trust Network helps merchants, issuers, acquirers, and processors collaborate through data sharing to prevent first-party and APP fraud. The network provides a 360 view of a consumer’s fraud risk for friendly fraud, without exposing personal or transactional data.

At its core, the Consumer Trust Index is a score that identifies trusted customers and differentiates them from potential fraudsters. This score provides companies with a view of how their customers act beyond their network, enabling the detection of fraudsters operating outside their network before they cause harm.

With the Consumer Trust Network, companies can make more effective reimbursement/refund decisions, resolve disputes faster and with less manual work, and prevent policy abuse, whilst preventing fraud losses from friendly fraud. By helping companies identify trustworthy customers and fraudsters, the Trust Index also supports businesses build trust with loyal customers and support growth.

The Trust Index is built using fraud insights shared by network members, combined with Open Banking and third-party data to close the visibility gap in fraud prevention. Through the Trust Network Protocol, peers can securely share and access consumer fraud risk insights while keeping the underlying data private. Members gain the benefits of shared intelligence without seeing the personal or transactional data behind it.

Unlike traditional systems that centralise data, Trudenty leverages shared infrastructure, so businesses keep control and ownership of their data. This type of open network enables data sharing of fraud risk signals whilst ensuring privacy and maintaining confidentiality for network members and consumers.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).

Cresora Commerce is an AI-native commerce infrastructure platform built for organizations operating in complex, high-volume, and regulated environments.

Modern commerce has outgrown traditional payment systems. Businesses today manage multiple transaction channels, fragmented financial data, and increasing pressure for speed, accuracy, and auditability. Legacy platforms were not designed for this level of complexity. They process transactions, but they do not orchestrate them.

Cresora solves this by acting as the infrastructure layer that connects systems, orchestrates transaction flow, and reconciles financial activity across the entire commerce lifecycle.

The platform unifies embedded commerce, omnichannel interaction, and financial reconciliation into a single framework. It enables organizations to route transactions across multiple processors, align data across systems, and achieve financial accuracy without manual reconciliation or rigid dependencies.

AI is embedded at the core of Cresora, powering data normalization, transaction matching, anomaly detection, and operational insights. This reduces manual work, accelerates financial close, and improves visibility across operations.

Cresora is processor-agnostic and bank-agnostic, giving organizations the flexibility to scale without being locked into a single provider. Its modular architecture supports enterprises, software platforms, and partner ecosystems that require control, compliance, and precision.

By transforming fragmented systems into a unified infrastructure, Cresora enables organizations to move money more intelligently, operate more efficiently, and achieve financial truth at scale.

The Challenge: Trapped Value
Over $2 trillion in global digital assets (crypto, stocks, loyalty points, etc.) is often locked, unusable for everyday spending at POS, online, or ATMs. This limits users and represents missed engagement opportunities for asset platforms.

Our Solution: The Middleware Bridge
goSettle provides essential 𝗺𝗶𝗱𝗱𝗹𝗲𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝗳𝗿𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲: a secure bridge connecting digital assets & payments. Our 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁 𝗮𝗴𝗻𝗼𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗰 platform works if the Asset Provider (AP) can validate ownership and convert the asset's value to FIAT. goSettle is 𝗻𝗼𝗻 𝗰𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗱𝗶𝗮𝗹 tech; we never hold client or partner funds.

How It Works (Simplified)
User initiates payment ➔ authorizes via their 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗔𝗣 app ➔ AP validates, converts asset to FIAT, confirms to goSettle ➔ goSettle relays instruction ➔ 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗿𝗲𝗴𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗣𝗮𝘆𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗻𝗲𝗿 executes 𝗴𝘂𝗮𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝗙𝗜𝗔𝗧 𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗹𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁. Result: Recipient gets FIAT seamlessly; consumer pays with their chosen asset.

Connecting the Ecosystem
Our ecosystem connects via secure APIs:
• 𝗔𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀: Exchanges, Brokers, Loyalty Programs, Banks, Gaming Platforms, etc.
• 𝗣𝗮𝘆𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀: PSPs (for merchants) & ATM Networks (for cash).

Value Delivered
• 𝗔𝗣𝘀: Unlock value, boost engagement & revenue, save costs vs DIY.
• 𝗣𝗮𝘆𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀: Differentiate, attract clients, simplify digital asset access.
• 𝗠𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝘁𝘀: Access new liquidity, get guaranteed FIAT risk free.
• 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘂𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀: Gain ultimate payment flexibility and convenience.

𝗦𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗲 & 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗯𝘆 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻

entity.name: Finexus
entity.description:
Finexus – Where Banks Meet Innovation

Finexus is a next-generation Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that empowers banks and fintech companies to launch new digital financial services faster, securely, and at scale.

Built on more than a decade of Al Faris International Group’s leadership in mission-critical banking integrations, Finexus offers 260+ Saudi-ready APIs that cover payments, lending, deposits, cards, wallets, trade finance, supply chain finance, payroll, collections, investments, and more. These APIs are fully aligned with Open Banking, Open Finance, and ISO 20022 standards, ensuring compliance with SAMA regulations and global frameworks.

Finexus is multi-tenant by design. This means individual bank departments (retail, corporate, SME) can run their own APIs with full data isolation, while external fintechs and third-party providers can also host services on the same platform under secure governance and revenue-sharing models.

The platform comes with a full ecosystem of tools:
Developer Portal – Interactive API documentation, sandbox testing, SDKs, and developer support.
Self-Service Portal for TPPs – Onboarding, consent and credential management, real-time analytics, and regulatory compliance tools.
Admin Portal for Banks – TPP approval, API lifecycle management, monitoring, fraud detection, billing, and subscription management.
Advanced Modules – Consent management (web & mobile SDKs), analytics dashboards, charging & billing engines, and marketplace integration for fintech, insuretech, agritech, and more.

With its SaaS deployment model, Finexus can run on leading cloud infrastructures with active-active disaster recovery, ensuring reliability and scalability.

By combining speed, flexibility, compliance, and monetization, Finexus helps banks modernize their digital offerings, enables fintechs to innovate, and creates new revenue streams through an open financial marketplace.

entity.name: Cresora Commerce
entity.description:
Cresora Commerce is an AI-native commerce infrastructure platform built for organizations operating in complex, high-volume, and regulated environments.

Modern commerce has outgrown traditional payment systems. Businesses today manage multiple transaction channels, fragmented financial data, and increasing pressure for speed, accuracy, and auditability. Legacy platforms were not designed for this level of complexity. They process transactions, but they do not orchestrate them.

Cresora solves this by acting as the infrastructure layer that connects systems, orchestrates transaction flow, and reconciles financial activity across the entire commerce lifecycle.

The platform unifies embedded commerce, omnichannel interaction, and financial reconciliation into a single framework. It enables organizations to route transactions across multiple processors, align data across systems, and achieve financial accuracy without manual reconciliation or rigid dependencies.

AI is embedded at the core of Cresora, powering data normalization, transaction matching, anomaly detection, and operational insights. This reduces manual work, accelerates financial close, and improves visibility across operations.

Cresora is processor-agnostic and bank-agnostic, giving organizations the flexibility to scale without being locked into a single provider. Its modular architecture supports enterprises, software platforms, and partner ecosystems that require control, compliance, and precision.

By transforming fragmented systems into a unified infrastructure, Cresora enables organizations to move money more intelligently, operate more efficiently, and achieve financial truth at scale.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for

business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.

    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
